desc: Prove the reduction: any valid kept subgraph corresponds to choosing a center c, a common D=y+1>=2, and c-neighbors v with deg(v)>=D; conversely such choices always form a Snowflake Tree since subtrees hanging off distinct c-neighbors are disjoint in a tree.

Implement the O(N) vertex-activation sweep: bucket vertices by degree, process degree d from maxDeg down to 2, for each v in bucket increment cnt[c] for every neighbor c and take max of 1+d*cnt[c]; answer N - max.
Confirm tie handling: evaluate after every increment so the full count D*cnt(c,D) is captured when the last same-degree neighbor is processed; deg(v)>=2 excludes leaves as intermediates.
Test against all three provided samples (results 1, 0, 3) — SAMPLE TESTS: PASSED all 3.
Verify input parsing handles N up to 3e5, code is non-recursive, and output is exactly the integer.
Confirm the optimal D for a fixed center equals some neighbor's degree (breakpoint argument), so the descending-degree sweep is exact.
Verify leaf-as-center cases (e.g. star K1,t gives best=n, answer 0) are covered by the sweep considering every neighbor c of a high-degree vertex v.
